I’ll trace scorer loading and guardrail validation, then add the server-side restriction and focused tests. I’m using the repository’s Python style skill for this change.
The working tree already contains regression tests for this behavior. I’ll preserve them and implement the restriction at scorer reconstruction. Guardrail loading will also get a distinct error for custom scorers, so those requests fail while unrelated loading failures keep their current skip-and-log behavior.
The scorer and guardrail tests are passing so far. Custom scorers now load as metadata in the server, preserving the fields needed for scheduling and forwarding. I also added scheduler filtering so a disabled custom scorer cannot prevent built-in scorers from being scheduled. Next I’m checking HTTP error behavior and workspace-aware guardrail creation.
All 63 selected guardrail, gateway API, and startup checks passed, including workspace-enabled cases. The broader focused run had one job-runner timeout; pytest’s final diagnostics also hit a sandbox permission error. I’m investigating the timeout and checking the added ensemble and source-evaluation regressions.
The focused checks now report 251 passed and 18 skipped, including serialization compatibility, custom-scorer refusal, ensemble rejection, and the executor entry point. The remaining job-runner integration test still times out; I’m checking its subprocess output to identify why.
Implemented inert custom-scorer loading in the server, with reconstruction blocked and executor permission cleared at startup. Executor and client behavior remain intact.

Custom guardrails—including ensembles—are rejected. Existing ones fail requests with HTTP 500 naming the guardrail; unrelated loading failures still log and skip.

Validation: 252 focused tests passed, 18 skipped. One job-runner integration test timed out. No dependencies installed or full suite run.
